s1.syndrome_frame: asymptomatic cardiac abnormality with murmur in a young adult
salient_findings: systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
complete right bundle-branch block on ECG
dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
key_facts: 29-year-old primigravida woman
no history of dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, or lower limb swelling
vital parameters within normal limits
systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
normal sinus rhythm with heart rate of 70 beats/min on ECG
complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
fragmented QRS with a notch on the R wave in inferior leads on ECG
no significant ST-T segment changes on ECG
dilated right atrium and right ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography
large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on transthoracic echocardiography
normal cardiac output on right-sided heart catheterization
step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium
pulmonary vascular resistance: 1.8 Wood units

shortlist.label: Atrial septal defect
shortlist.why_kept: Large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on transthoracic echocardiography

shortlist.label: Ventricular septal defect
shortlist.why_kept: Step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium on right-sided heart catheterization

shortlist.label: Sinus venosus atrial septal defect
shortlist.why_kept: Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography

shortlist.label: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal oxygenation step-up on right-sided heart catheterization

shortlist.label: Scimitar syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Anomalous pulmonary venous connection suggested by abnormal oxygenation and echocardiography findings

raw.rationale: The presence of a large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on transthoracic echocardiography, along with a step-up in oxygenation from the superior vena cava to the right atrium, is consistent with an atrial septal defect.

rejected.label: Ventricular septal defect
rejected.why: The echocardiogram specifically mentions a large defect with left-to-right shunt, which is more characteristic of an atrial septal defect than a ventricular septal defect.

rejected.label: Sinus venosus atrial septal defect
rejected.why: While possible, the information provided does not specifically suggest the defect is located at the junction of the superior vena cava with the right atrium, which is typical for sinus venosus defects.

rejected.label: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection
rejected.why: There is no mention of anomalous pulmonary veins connecting to the right atrium or its tributaries, which would be expected in this condition.

rejected.label: Scimitar syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves anomalous pulmonary venous return to the inferior vena cava, which is not indicated by the provided findings.
